section: International environmental treaties - Stockholm 1972, Rio 1992, Ramsar, CITES, CBD and its protocols
subsections: Rio Earth Summit 1992 - name, venue, documents, Rio+5, Rio+20
CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the outputs of the Rio Earth Summit, 1992:
1. The Rio Declaration contains 27 principles on environment and development.
2. The Forest Principles constitute a legally binding convention on forests.
3. Agenda 21 is an action plan for sustainable development at all levels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Forest Principles are a non-binding statement, not a legally binding convention.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement by checking the legal status of the Forest Principles.
accepted.sec: Rio Earth Summit 1992 - name, venue, documents, Rio+5, Rio+20  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs of instruments was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit, 1992?
accepted.x: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Convention on Biological Diversity were opened for signature at Rio in 1992.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair of agreements associated with the Rio Summit itself.
accepted.sec: Rio Earth Summit 1992 - name, venue, documents, Rio+5, Rio+20  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Adoption of the UNCCD
B. Rio Earth Summit
C. Rio+5 review
D. Rio+20 Conference
accepted.x: The Rio Earth Summit was held in 1992, Rio+5 in 1997, the UNCCD was adopted in 1994, and Rio+20 took place in 2012. Therefore, strictly by year the correct order is Rio Summit, UNCCD adoption, Rio+5, Rio+20; however, the provided option sequence does not reflect that order. The correct chronological sequence should be B, A, C, D.
accepted.tq: Place the dated events first and verify the middle two events carefully.
accepted.sec: Rio Earth Summit 1992 - name, venue, documents, Rio+5, Rio+20  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rio+5, held in 1997, primarily involved which of the following?
o: A special session of the UN General Assembly reviewing Agenda 21
Establishment of the UNEA at Nairobi
accepted.x: Rio+5 was a special session of the United Nations General Assembly held in New York in 1997 to review the implementation of Agenda 21.
accepted.tq: Match the review conference with its specific institutional setting and subject.
accepted.sec: Rio Earth Summit 1992 - name, venue, documents, Rio+5, Rio+20  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Rio+20, consider the following statements:
1. Its outcome document was titled ‘The Future We Want’.
2. It launched the process that led to the Sustainable Development Goals.
3. It established the UN Environment Assembly with universal membership.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Rio+20 in 2012 produced ‘The Future We Want’, initiated the SDG process and established the UNEA with universal membership.
accepted.tq: When all three statements describe major outcomes of the same summit, test the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Rio Earth Summit 1992 - name, venue, documents, Rio+5, Rio+20  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA), established as an outcome of Rio+20, has which of the following characteristics?
o: It has 193 members and meets biennially in Nairobi.
It has universal membership and meets every four years in New York.
It has 27 members and meets annually in Geneva.
It consists only of Rio Convention parties and meets biennially in Montreal.
accepted.x: UNEA has universal membership of 193 countries and meets every two years in Nairobi.
accepted.tq: Separate the body’s membership, meeting frequency and venue from those of other environmental institutions.
accepted.sec: Rio Earth Summit 1992 - name, venue, documents, Rio+5, Rio+20  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity?
o: Sustainable use of the components of biodiversity
Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies to developing countries
Fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources
accepted.x: The CBD objectives are conservation, sustainable use and fair and equitable benefit-sharing. Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies is not one of its objectives.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that extends the treaty beyond its stated three-objective structure.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Convention on Biological Diversity:
1. It was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992.
2. It entered into force in 1993.
3. Its Secretariat is located in Montreal, Canada.
4. India ratified it in 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The CBD was opened at Rio in 1992, entered into force in 1993, has its Secretariat in Montreal and was ratified by India in 1994.
accepted.tq: Check treaty facts in the order of adoption, entry into force, headquarters and national ratification.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity was held at:
accepted.x: The first CBD COP was held at Nassau, Bahamas, in 1994.
accepted.tq: Use the earliest COP number to identify the earliest venue in the list.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Instrument)
a. Cartagena Protocol
b. Nagoya Protocol
c. Aichi Targets
d. Kunming-Montreal GBF

List-II (Subject or feature)
i. Access and benefit-sharing
 ii. Biosafety and living modified organisms
 iii. Twenty targets for 2011–2020
 iv. Four goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030
accepted.x: Cartagena concerns biosafety, Nagoya concerns access and benefit-sharing, the Aichi Targets numbered 20 for 2011–2020, and the Kunming-Montreal GBF contains four 2050 goals and 23 targets for 2030.
accepted.tq: Begin with the distinctive subject of Cartagena and eliminate codes that swap the protocols.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Kunming-Montreal GBF — adopted in 2000 and entered into force in 2003
Cartagena Protocol — adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014
Nagoya Protocol — adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014
Aichi Targets — adopted in 2022 for the period 2030–2050
accepted.x: The Nagoya Protocol was adopted in 2010 at COP-10 and entered into force in 2014. Cartagena was adopted in 2000 and entered into force in 2003, while the Aichi Targets and GBF have different dates.
accepted.tq: Check each instrument against its adoption and entry-into-force dates rather than relying on the protocol names alone.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety primarily deals with:
o: Protection of wetlands of international importance
Fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources
Safe transfer of living modified organisms
accepted.x: The Cartagena Protocol deals with biosafety and the safe transfer of living modified organisms.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Cartagena’s biosafety function from Nagoya’s access-and-benefit-sharing function.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Aichi Targets were associated with which of the following?
o: 23 targets for 2030, adopted at COP-15 in 2022
17 targets for 2030, adopted at Rio in 1992
20 targets for 2011–2020, adopted at COP-10 in 2010
Four goals for 2050, adopted at COP-16 in 2024
accepted.x: The Aichi Targets comprised 20 targets for 2011–2020 and were adopted at CBD COP-10 in 2010.
accepted.tq: Pair the target count and time period before checking the COP number and year.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, consider the following statements:
1. It contains four goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030.
2. It was adopted at COP-15 in December 2022.
3. It includes the 30x30 objective.
4. It seeks to halve food waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The framework has four 2050 goals, 23 targets for 2030, the 30x30 objective and a target to halve food waste.
accepted.tq: Test the numerical framework together with its major action targets.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the 30x30 objective of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the target is to protect by 2030:
accepted.x: The 30x30 objective seeks protection of 30 per cent of the world’s land and oceans by 2030.
accepted.tq: Read the numerical shorthand literally and avoid replacing the combined land-and-ocean target with forests alone.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following targets is associated with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework?
o: Increase harmful subsidies by 500 billion dollars per year
Cut harmful subsidies by 500 billion dollars per year
Eliminate all international trade in genetic resources by 2030
Restore only 3 per cent of degraded ecosystems
accepted.x: The framework seeks to cut harmful subsidies by 500 billion dollars annually and also aims to restore 30 per cent of degraded ecosystems.
accepted.tq: Use the direction of the policy target—cut rather than increase—as the key distinction.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: COP-15 of the Convention on Biological Diversity is correctly associated with which combination?
o: Cali and Rome, 2024–2025 — Cali Fund on DSI
accepted.x: COP-15 began in Kunming in 2021 and concluded in Montreal in December 2022, producing the Kunming-Montreal GBF. The other combinations refer to COP-1, COP-10 and COP-16 respectively.
accepted.tq: Match the COP number with its host sequence and principal outcome.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding COP-15 of the Convention on Biological Diversity:
1. It also served as the tenth Meeting of the Parties to the Cartagena Protocol.
2. It also served as the fourth Meeting of the Parties to the Nagoya Protocol.
3. It resulted in the establishment of the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund under the GEF.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: COP-15 also functioned as the 10th MOP of Cartagena and the 4th MOP of Nagoya, and it was associated with the GBF Fund under the GEF.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional labels and outcomes that occurred at the same COP.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence of events relating to CBD COP-16?
o: It was held at Cali in 2024 and resumed at Rome in February 2025.
It was held at Montreal in 2022 and resumed at Nairobi in 2023.
It was held at Nagoya in 2010 and resumed at Kunming in 2021.
It was held at Hyderabad in 2012 and resumed at Sharm El Sheikh in 2018.
accepted.x: CBD COP-16 was held at Cali, Colombia, in October–November 2024 and resumed at Rome in February 2025.
accepted.tq: Track the host city first and then verify the resumed session and year.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The COP of the Convention on Biological Diversity held in Hyderabad in 2012 was:
accepted.x: Hyderabad, India, hosted CBD COP-11 in 2012.
accepted.tq: Use the host-year pairing to distinguish India’s COP-11 from the other listed COPs.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Nagoya Protocol is correct?
o: It concerns only the transboundary movement of hazardous waste.
It established the 20 Aichi Targets for 2011–2020.
It regulates wetlands listed under the Ramsar Convention.
It concerns access and benefit-sharing from the utilisation of genetic resources.
accepted.x: The Nagoya Protocol establishes the framework for access and fair benefit-sharing arising from the utilisation of genetic resources.
accepted.tq: Separate the access-and-benefit-sharing protocol from biosafety and wetland instruments.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The financial mechanism associated with the Convention on Biological Diversity, and also with the UNFCCC, is the:
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
accepted.x: The Global Environment Facility serves as a financial mechanism for both the CBD and the UNFCCC.
accepted.tq: Identify the common financial institution rather than a treaty body or conservation network.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Article 26 of the Convention on Biological Diversity is associated with the requirement of:
o: A permanent ban on genetic-resource utilisation
Annual meetings of all national parliaments
accepted.x: Article 26 requires Parties to submit national reports, generally at intervals of about four years.
accepted.tq: Match the article number with the reporting obligation rather than with a substantive conservation target.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s first National Report on the Nagoya Protocol recorded approximately how many Biodiversity Management Committees?
accepted.x: India’s first National Report on the Nagoya Protocol recorded approximately 2.76 lakh Biodiversity Management Committees.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the lakh-scale committee figure from the separate certificate count.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s first National Report on the Nagoya Protocol reported how many Certificates of Compliance, representing more than 60 per cent of the global total?
accepted.x: The report recorded 3,556 Certificates of Compliance, stated to be more than 60 per cent of the global total.
accepted.tq: Keep the exact certificate count separate from the much larger Biodiversity Management Committee count.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The seventh National Report to the CBD is significant because it provides:
o: The first assessment of the 20 Aichi Targets for 2011–2020
The first global inventory of Ramsar wetlands
The first full assessment against the 23 Kunming-Montreal GBF targets
The first report on the Stockholm Declaration
accepted.x: India’s seventh National Report to the CBD is the first full assessment against the 23 targets of the Kunming-Montreal GBF.
accepted.tq: Link the report number with the newer 23-target framework rather than the earlier Aichi framework.
accepted.sec: CBD protocols and targets - Cartagena, Nagoya, Aichi, Kunming-Montreal  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, 1972, was held at:
accepted.x: The UN Conference on the Human Environment was held in Stockholm, Sweden, from 5 to 16 June 1972.
accepted.tq: Use the official conference name to distinguish Stockholm 1972 from UNCED 1992.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Conference 1972 - name, venue, outcomes, India  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following were outcomes of the Stockholm Conference, 1972?
1. Stockholm Declaration containing 26 principles
2. An Action Plan
3. Establishment of UNEP
4. Recognition of 5 June as World Environment Day
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Stockholm Conference produced the 26-principle Stockholm Declaration and an Action Plan, led to the establishment of UNEP and resulted in 5 June being observed as World Environment Day.
accepted.tq: Group the declaration, institutional outcome, action plan and commemorative date as conference results.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Conference 1972 - name, venue, outcomes, India  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme, established in 1972, is located at:
accepted.x: UNEP was established in 1972 and its headquarters is in Nairobi, Kenya.
accepted.tq: Distinguish UNEP’s headquarters from the venue of the Stockholm Conference and the CBD Secretariat.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Conference 1972 - name, venue, outcomes, India  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to India’s participation in the Stockholm Conference, consider the following statements:
1. Prime Minister Indira Gandhi attended the Conference.
2. She linked poverty with environmental concerns.
3. India was described as a cautious participant at Stockholm.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Indira Gandhi attended Stockholm, connected poverty and environment, and India’s role was described as that of a cautious participant.
accepted.tq: Check the leader, the central argument and the characterization of India’s participation together.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Conference 1972 - name, venue, outcomes, India  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the context of the Stockholm Conference, the significance attributed to Indira Gandhi was that she was:
o: The author of the Rio Declaration
The chairperson of the CBD COP-1
The only visiting head of government to attend the Conference
accepted.x: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was described as the only visiting head of government who attended the Stockholm Conference.
accepted.tq: Use the unique-status phrase to distinguish the participant from later environmental office-holders.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Conference 1972 - name, venue, outcomes, India  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The decisions of the Stockholm Conference in India were implemented through the:
accepted.x: The Stockholm decisions were implemented in India through the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
accepted.tq: Match the international conference outcome with the specific Indian legal instrument.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Conference 1972 - name, venue, outcomes, India  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following comparisons between the Stockholm Conference and the Rio Earth Summit is correct?
o: Stockholm established the CBD, whereas Rio established the UNEP in 1972.
Stockholm 1972 concerned the human environment, whereas Rio 1992 concerned environment and development.
Stockholm 1992 concerned biodiversity, whereas Rio 1972 concerned human rights.
Both were held in Rio de Janeiro and produced the same declaration.
accepted.x: The 1972 Stockholm Conference was the UN Conference on the Human Environment, while the 1992 Rio Summit was UNCED, focused on environment and development.
accepted.tq: Compare the official names and years before comparing their institutional outcomes.
accepted.sec: Stockholm Conference 1972 - name, venue, outcomes, India  [APPSC]
